description:
## Problem
After the withdrawal the old run path still works and would produce a non-specification result marked PASSED. A run with no validation evidence is labelled passed today. This step is where the old run path stops.

## Owner decisions (choice dialogs, 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-21)
- Refusal message, exactly: "TPC-DI is unavailable while BenchBox reworks it to run the specification's workload (historical load, two incremental updates, automated audit). Earlier BenchBox TPC-DI results were withdrawn." Exit code 2.
- Registry status: "`document_only` during the rework; `experimental` once DuckDB passes the full audit; `beta` only when at least three platforms pass it."
- "`--official` with TPC-DI is refused."
- "Old TPC-DI bundles a user still has load read-only as legacy and 'not validated'; compare, publish and submit refuse them."
- "UAT: TPC-DI is excluded through the registry status; the TPC-DI-specific prune rules are deleted."
- "'No validation evidence means not passed' applies to TPC-DI now; the same rule for other benchmarks is filed as a separate item."
- Old generator and ETL code stays in place, unreachable: "Keep to the letter: delete only after the DuckDB historical load passes its audit; the dead code is excluded from tests meanwhile."
- "the registry shows 0 queries while TPC-DI is unavailable."
- 2026-11-21, old-path tests: "Delete the tests of the old path in that PR, listed in its body." 
- 2026-11-21, texts: registry description "TPC-DI data integration benchmark. Unavailable while BenchBox reworks it to run the specification's workload." Shown for an old bundle "Legacy TPC-DI result from a withdrawn workload; not validated."

## Change
Registry status `document_only`, new description, num_queries 0. One refusal check in core/run_service.py used by the run command, the MCP tool, the benchbox/tpcdi.py facade and TPCDIBenchmark's public entry points (generate_data, run_full_benchmark, run_etl_benchmark, calculate_official_metrics, execute_dataframe_workload). Result builder: a tpcdi result without a TPC-DI audit block is NOT_VALIDATED. Loader marks old TPC-DI bundles legacy. UAT matrix skips the status; delete the TPC-DI prune rules and their tests. Breaking changelog fragment. Entry points also include the dry-run path (`cli/commands/run.py` into `cli/dryrun.py`, which names TPCDI) and the MCP discovery and query tools (`mcp/tools/discovery.py` calls `get_queries`; `get_query_details`): each refuses or reports TPC-DI as unavailable with 0 queries, and the MCP run tool's description string no longer advertises TPC-DI. Tests that call the old path are deleted here and listed in the pull request body (at least `tests/test_tpcdi.py`, `tests/integration/test_tpcdi_*.py`, and the TPC-DI cases in `tests/unit/test_wrapper_classes.py`, `tests/unit/test_error_handling.py`, `tests/utilities/benchmark_validator.py`); cross-benchmark parametrised tests exempt `tpcdi` through the registry status, not by a hard-coded name list where a status check is possible. Regenerate the fast-tier duration baseline with its own command if the deleted tests change it.

## Decision gates
The breaking changelog entry's text is shown in the pull request description. If any result-construction path bypasses the builder, add the rule there and a test per constructor; if one cannot be covered, stop and report. Do not delete the old generator, ETL or query modules here. The registry description and the legacy-bundle wording are the owner's texts, used verbatim. If the diff (deleted tests plus the regenerated fast-tier duration baseline) would exceed the review bot's limit of about 20,000 changed lines or 300 files, stop and report the sizes before opening the pull request; the baseline is regenerated only by its documented procedure (name it in the pull request).

## Verification rubric
Pass, each by a test that fails before the change: `benchbox run --benchmark tpcdi` (CliRunner) exits 2 with the exact message; the MCP run tool refuses; each listed Python entry point raises with the message; a tpcdi result with no audit block is NOT_VALIDATED and `publish_admission` returns non_clean; an old TPC-DI bundle loads as legacy and is refused by compare, publish and submit; `--official` with tpcdi is refused; the UAT resolver omits tpcdi. `make pr-preflight` exits 0. The pull request states which old modules remain and that nothing reaches them. Also by test: `benchbox run --benchmark tpcdi --dry-run <tmpdir>` exits 2 with the message; `benchbox datagen --benchmark tpcdi` exits 2 with the message; the registry description and the legacy wording equal the owner's texts; the MCP discovery and query-detail tools return no TPC-DI query and state the status; no test file deleted here is still collected (`uv run -- pytest --collect-only -q | rg -c tpcdi` is compared before and after and the difference is explained in the pull request).

## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-21)
- The agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`.
- Arming: `make pr-arm` once; one more attempt only when the refusal named a cause, the agent reported it and the cause is cleared; never a third without asking. `make pr-rerun` at most once and only for a job the runner never ran or cancelled, never for a failed test.
- Review threads: reply; resolve only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise the finding again.
- Subagents are read-only. No file edit by script; use the edit tool. Do not edit a pull request description while its CI is starting; post a comment.
- Any limit, default, threshold, status token, message, label text or name (option, configuration key, result field, file name, test hook) the owner has not already chosen is chosen by the implementer following existing BenchBox conventions and the specification, and is listed in the pull request (owner, 2026-11-21: no stop for these). Texts the owner has chosen (see tpcdi-correction-plan-20261120) are used verbatim.
- A blocked step stops this item; no workaround. No live cloud run. Heavy work only through `make heavy-run`. Delivery follows the batch plan on tpcdi-correction-plan-20261120: a batch member ends at a landing report and its batch has one final pull request; a serial item has its own pull request.
- From the quarantine step until the reopening step, no TPC-DI entry point may produce a result that reads PASSED or is admitted for publication.
- Sources. SQL derived from the Databricks project (`src/incremental_batches/**` at commit 8e0f944, treated as MIT on the owner's instruction) may be committed only after the provenance step has merged, only under `benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/`, with every file listed in `PROVENANCE.json` and with all comments removed.
- TPC and bankmark files (DIGen, PDGF, dictionaries, configuration, EULA, appendix SQL) come only from the official archive the owner supplies, are committed unmodified and only in `_sources/tpc-di/`, `benchbox/_binaries/tpc-di/` and `benchbox/_binaries/tpc-di/tools/`. Never copy from the Databricks project or the DuckDB implementation: their copies of the tools or the tools zip, DIGen output, generated reference files, audit snapshots, their copy or rewrite of the appendix SQL, or any generator code (`src/tools/**`). Never commit DIGen output.
- The specification wins over the Databricks project without asking. Each behaviour of the project that is kept and each change made to follow the specification is one row in `benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/DEPARTURES.yaml`, which the owner approves at the milestone stop.
- Owner, 2026-11-21: "The specification wins without asking. Every difference, and any behaviour of the project that is kept, goes in a catalogue I approve at the milestone stop. A difference from the DuckDB implementation not in the catalogue is a finding that blocks the step." The catalogue is `DEPARTURES.yaml`; every entry of the comparison's expected-differences list must cite a catalogue row. After the milestone stop, a new catalogue row in which BenchBox follows the specification is listed in the pull request; a row that would keep behaviour of the Databricks project that departs from the specification stops for the owner's approval (owner, 2026-11-21).
- The agent never contacts bankmark, the TPC or the Databricks project's author.
- Staging files produced by DIGen are never edited. The official audit, validation and visibility SQL is never edited in the repository.
